newsitem.title: USA: States sue contact lens makers.
newsitem.headline: States sue contact lens makers.

text.p: Twenty-two states filed an antitrust suit against contact lens companies and a national optometric association on Thursday alleging they conspired to eliminate the supply of contact lens to lower priced retail outlets.
The suit, filed in Brooklyn federal court, names as defendants Vistakon, a unit of Johnson & Johnson Bausch & Lomb Inc. and CIBA Vision Corp.
The suit also names the American Optometric Association as well as eight optometrists.
"This lawsuit is without merit and (we) will vigorously contest it," Johnson & Johnson said.
The suit alleges that the defendants conspired to restrict consumer access to prescriptions they need to obtain replacement lenses from from distributors other than licensed eye care professionals.
Alternate distributors include mail order companies, pharmacies, buying clubs, department stores and mass merchandise outlets.

The lawsuit also alleges the contact lens industry has sought to eliminate the alternative distributors who sell lenses at lower prices or make it more costly for the distributors to operate. The alleged practice results in artificially-high prices for replacing lenses, the suit said.

The states alleged that following the introduction of disposable contact lenses into the market, the industry attempted to limit the sale of the lenses by anyone other than licensed eye care professionals.
Contact lens manufacturers allegedly agreed to supply only eye care professionals, and developed almost identical policies against selling lenses to alternative distributors.
Manufacturers also allegedly enforced the policies in response to optometrists demands, the suit alleged.

"Through these alleged tactics, the contact lens industry attempted to limit consumers' access to affordable replacement lenses and drive up the cost to benefit themselves," said Massachusetts Attorney General Scott Harshbarger.
Johnson & Johnson refuted this saying that Vistakon independently established a policy of distributing its lenses only to licensed eye care professionals who fit contact lenses on their premises.
The policy was not intended to drive up prices, Johnson & Johnson contended.

"This policy was adopted to ensure marketplace acceptance of the product, particularly acceptance by eye care professionals and to ensure optimum eye healthy for wears of our contact lenses," the company said.
